items.q: Match the following diabetes subtype — 1) LADA 2) Type 3c (pancreatogenic) 3) Type 4 (gestational) 4) MODY … A) Slow autoimmune diabetes in adults B) Diabetes following pancreatic disease C) Diabetes diagnosed in pregnancy D) Monogenic autosomal dominant diabetes
items.exp: LADA is slow autoimmune diabetes in adults; type 3c is pancreatogenic diabetes after pancreatic disease; type 4 is gestational diabetes; MODY is monogenic autosomal dominant diabetes. (Book p921)

items.q: A 38-year-old non-obese patient with GAD positivity initially responds to metformin but progresses to insulin within 4 years. The most consistent label is:
items.exp: Slow autoimmune diabetes in non-obese adults progressing to insulin fits LADA; MODY would be antibody negative and autosomal dominant. (Book p921)

items.q: Assess LADA: I GAD, IA-2 and ZnT8 antibodies can be present. II Patients usually avoid insulin for years.
items.exp: LADA shares the same antibody panel as Type 1 diabetes; patients often avoid insulin for months to a few years but progress. (Book p921)

items.q: Which is the odd one out — a feature of LADA rather than Type 2 diabetes?
items.exp: Obesity with central adiposity is characteristic of Type 2; LADA features persistent antibodies, non-obese phenotype and earlier insulin need. (Book p921)

items.q: Type 3c diabetes (pancreatogenic) is most commonly due to chronic ___ in adults.
items.exp: Chronic pancreatitis is the most common cause of pancreatogenic diabetes; cystic fibrosis, pancreatic cancer and haemochromatosis are other causes. (Book p921)

items.q: Match the following diabetes subtype to its key clue — 1) MODY 2 (GCK) 2) MODY 3 (HNF1A) 3) Mitochondrial diabetes 4) Wolfram syndrome … A) Mild stable hyperglycaemia, low Rx need B) Progressive sulfonylurea-responsive C) Maternal inheritance with deafness D) Diabetes insipidus, optic atrophy, deafness
items.exp: MODY 2 (GCK) is mild; MODY 3 (HNF1A) is sulfonylurea-responsive; mitochondrial diabetes shows maternal inheritance with deafness; Wolfram syndrome has DI, optic atrophy and deafness (DIDMOAD). (Book p921)

items.q: A young patient with diabetes also has sensorineural deafness and a maternal family history. The most likely diagnosis is:
items.exp: Maternal inheritance with diabetes and deafness fits mitochondrial diabetes (MIDD, MELAS-related). (Book p921)

items.q: Assess Wolfram syndrome: I It includes diabetes insipidus, optic atrophy and deafness. II It is also called DIDMOAD.
items.exp: Wolfram syndrome (DIDMOAD) is characterised by DI, optic atrophy, deafness and diabetes mellitus. (Book p921)

items.q: Match the following subtype to its antibody / genetic marker — 1) LADA 2) MODY 3 3) Type 3c (pancreatogenic) 4) Mitochondrial … A) GAD antibody positive B) HNF1A mutation C) Anti-GAD negative, exocrine insufficiency D) mtDNA 3243A>G mutation
items.exp: LADA is GAD-positive; MODY 3 has HNF1A mutation; pancreatogenic diabetes is GAD-negative with exocrine insufficiency; mitochondrial diabetes is associated with the 3243A>G mutation. (Book p921)

items.q: A 45-year-old with chronic pancreatitis and new diabetes has low C-peptide and steatorrhoea. The most consistent diagnosis is:
items.exp: Diabetes following chronic pancreatitis with low C-peptide and exocrine insufficiency fits type 3c pancreatogenic diabetes. (Book p921)

items.q: Type 3c diabetes is associated with both endocrine and ___ insufficiency.
items.exp: Type 3c combines endocrine and exocrine pancreatic insufficiency, distinguishing it from Type 2 diabetes. (Book p921)

items.q: Assess type 4 diabetes: I Gestational diabetes is diagnosed at 24–28 weeks. II Persisting after delivery is labelled GDM; resolving excludes future risk.
items.exp: GDM is typically screened at 24–28 weeks; persistence postpartum defines overt diabetes, and even resolving GDM signals long-term risk. (Book p921)
